title: Mocks + application sprint + capstone guardrails
objective: Two coding mocks + one system-design mock, recorded and reviewed; behavioral drill against the Googleyness & Leadership rubric; application pipeline (referrals first, direct second, 8–10 parallel companies). Capstone: guardrails + published red-team results.
topics: Capstone: guardrails, red-team suite, eval CI, public cost dashboard
AI-candidate depth: model choices, leakage, evals, production failure modes
deliverables: Application tracker ≥20 rows; ≥3 referral asks made
Capstone: guardrails + red-team results page; eval CI; public cost dashboard
checkpoint: Behavioral answers scored by a peer

practical: Red-team results published on the capstone

tasks.text: Coding mock 1 (Pramp/interviewing.io), recorded; debrief within the hour; drill the specific gap immediately (not “DSA in general”).
Tailor resume bullets per JD for 5 target postings (role family: SWE vs AI Eng); apply; tracker updated with matching evidence per minimum qualification.
Capstone: guardrails (topic allow-list, no PII, citation-required), red-team suite (injection via project docs, prompt extraction, off-topic abuse); publish results on the site.
Behavioral drill: 6 stories against Googleyness & Leadership (ownership, ambiguity, conflict, failure, impact, growth); a peer scores clarity, not just correctness.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Capstone: guardrails (topic allow-list, no PII, citation-required), red-team suite (inject” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
System-design mock (45 min): AI case (enterprise RAG platform or agent deployment). Record; delta.
AI-candidate depth prep: for each flagship, prepare answers on model choices, data leakage risks, evaluation design, production failure modes, and cost — one page.
Referral asks: for 3 Quiet Network contacts with real rapport, a specific easy “yes” (role id + resume + demo link). Log. Follow up on open applications politely.
Capstone: eval CI (recruiter golden set gate) + public cost/uptime dashboard.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Capstone: eval CI (recruiter golden set gate) + public cost/uptime dashboard” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
Coding mock 2, recorded; debrief; drill the gap.
Second-pass DSA: 4 cold re-solves from your weakest two categories.
Application pipeline (20 min): check saved searches, apply to 1–2 fitting roles within 48 h of posting, update tracker (status · next action · what failed).
Watch all three mock recordings back to back; write the top-3 patterns of failure and one concrete fix each for next week.
Apply to 5 more roles (parallel companies); tracker.

Weekly revision — Mocks: 2 coding + 1 SD, Behavioral drill: Googleyness & Leadership, Application pipeline + referral asks, Capstone: guardrails, red-team suite, eval CI, public cost dashboard: rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Decode Ways (Medium, B75) · Coin Change (Medium, B75) — ≤35 min each, narrate, log time.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.

JS/MERN spaced recall (Cycle 3 · interview mode) · React core: rendering, state, effects: Interview mode: 2-min answer ‘why does React re-render’, then machine-code a tabs or modal component in 20 min. Log misses in mistakes.md; if you fail the check, redo the matching module in Side Tracks → 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher.
Plan next week: read W50’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
